newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-PNG to raise A$260 mln from minerals float.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-PNG to raise A$260 mln from minerals float.

text.p: The Papua New Guinea Government would list a minority stake in its Mineral Resources Development Corp on the Australian Stock Exchange in early November after a A$260 million share raising from PNG and international investors, an underwriting source told Reuters on Wednesday.
The source said the PNG Government would continue to own 51 percent of Mineral Resources, with the other 49 percent to be held through a new company to be called Orogen Minerals Ltd.
Retail investors outside PNG would be offered Orogen shares at A$1.70 each, while PNG residents would receive a 10 percent discount on the the first 2,000 sharess.
The final price to be paid by institutional investors would depend on the range of bids made in a tender process.

Orogen Minerals would have a stake in some of PNG's largest gold and petroleum projects. The company will have a 20.5 percent stake in the Gobe oilfield, a 15.75 percent stake in Kutubu oilfied operated by Chevron Corp, a 15 percent stake in the Porgera gold mine operated by Placer Pacific Ltd, a 20 percent stake in Placer's Misima gold mine, and a 6.75 percent holding in the Lihir gold mine.
McIntosh Corporate Ltd and Jardine Fleming Ord Minnett have been appointed global joint managers of the float.
Co-managers of the share issue were HSBC James Capel, SBC Warburg, Wilson HTM and Morgan Stockbroking.
